title: Does every row of the table hold the same number of primes?
description: The ten rows of the table are read one at a time and the circled primes in each row are counted. The counts show which rows hold the least and the most primes.
teaching_notes: One idea: the primes are counted row by row, and a total that matches the number of primes in the whole table shows that no row was missed. Watch for students who count a crossed out number as a prime.

video_script.why: The child counts the circled numbers in each row of the finished table and compares the counts.
video_script.substitution: Count the circled numbers in each row, then compare the ten counts.
video_script.anchor: The finished table of 1 to 100 in ten rows, with the primes circled
video_script.payoff_line: No, the rows do not all hold the same number of primes.

final_answer.value: No. Least: 91 to 100. Most: 1 to 10 and 11 to 20
final_answer.spoken: the counts differ from row to row

maths_rules: the least is 1 in the row 91 to 100; the most is 4 in the rows 1 to 10 and 11 to 20
video_script.design: A bar of circled primes is drawn beside each row of the table; the shortest bar is amber and the longest bars are teal.
